VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed bound is $\lfloor (3t-1)/2 \rfloor$, and the sharpness example checks out. The problem is the upper bound. The argument for it is a sketch ("this forces a very rigid tiling structure," "trees, pendant tails, twin vertices... all destroy criticality") with no proof that a graph of larger diameter cannot have $\mathfrak m \in \operatorname{Ass}(R/NI(G)^t)$. The conclusion that only a single cycle $C_{3t-1}$ can work is asserted, not derived.

The sharpness example itself is correct. For $C_5$ with $t=2$, $f=x_1\cdots x_5$ has degree 5 < 6, so $f \notin NI^2$. Each $x_v f$ splits into two closed neighborhoods, so $NI^2 : f = \mathfrak m$. The same tiling works for $C_{3t-1}$ in general.

The upper bound is unverified, and I suspect it is too small. The natural analogues in the literature for this kind of result tend to be linear in $t$ with a larger coefficient (such as $2t$ or $3t-1$), and I could not rule out a graph with diameter exceeding $\lfloor (3t-1)/2 \rfloor$ that satisfies the condition. Checking $C_6$ for $t=2$ (diameter 3) was inconclusive: the natural candidate $f = x_1\cdots x_6$ lies in $NI^2$, and $f = x_1\cdots x_5$ fails at $v=1$.

CONFIDENCE: 2
